    57	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the point block of a uniformly random
    58	ambient vector is uniform. -/
    59	private theorem map_uniformDistribution_point (L : LdParams) :
    60	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point =
    61	      uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := by
    62	  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
    63	      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
    64	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
    65	  calc
    66	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point
    67	        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
    68	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by
    69	          rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
    70	          rfl
    71	    _ = ((uniformDistribution
    72	          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map
    73	            Prod.fst).map Prod.fst := by rw [hsplit]
    74	    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.fst := by
    75	          rw [uniformDistribution_map_fst]
    76	    _ = uniformDistribution (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) := uniformDistribution_map_fst
    77

    79	uniformly random ambient vector is uniform. -/

    83	  have hsplit : (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L) =
    84	      uniformDistribution (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L)) :=
    85	    uniformDistribution_map_equiv (ldSpaceSplit L)
    86	  calc
    87	    (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed
    88	        = (((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map (ldSpaceSplit L)).map
    89	            Prod.fst).map Prod.snd := by
    90	          rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]

    92	    _ = ((uniformDistribution
    93	          (((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L) × (Fin L.m → ScalarQ L))).map

    95	    _ = (uniformDistribution ((Fin L.m → ScalarQ L) × ScalarQ L)).map Prod.snd := by

    99	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: an admissible field size is positive. -/
   100	private theorem ldParams_q_pos (L : LdParams) : 0 < L.q := by
   101	  obtain ⟨j, -, hj⟩ := L.hq
   102	  rw [hj]
   103	  exact Nat.pow_pos (by norm_num)

   105	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: the coordinate index of a scalar is
   106	read off from its binary representation. -/
   107	private theorem chiIndex_eq_iff (L : LdParams) (s : ScalarQ L) (i : Fin L.m) :
   108	    chiIndex L s = i ↔
   109	      ((binaryRepresentation L.model s).val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val := by
   110	  rw [Fin.ext_iff]
   111	  simp [chiIndex]
   112	
   113	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary lemma: every fiber of the coordinate index has
   114	exactly `q / m` elements.  This is the balance property used in
   115	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`, paper
   116	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`. -/
   117	private theorem card_chiIndex_fiber (L : LdParams) (i : Fin L.m) :
   118	    ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   119	      = L.q / L.m := by
   120	  have hq : 0 < L.q := ldParams_q_pos L
   121	  have hqk : L.m * (L.q / L.m) = L.q := Nat.mul_div_cancel' L.hdvd
   122	  have hkpos : 0 < L.q / L.m := by
   123	    rcases Nat.eq_zero_or_pos (L.q / L.m) with h | h
   124	    · rw [h, Nat.mul_zero] at hqk
   125	      omega
   126	    · exact h
   127	  have hstep1 :
   128	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (ScalarQ L)).filter fun s => chiIndex L s = i).card
   129	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   130	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).card := by
   131	    refine Finset.card_equiv (binaryRepresentation L.model) fun s => ?_
   132	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, chiIndex_eq_iff]
   133	  have hstep2 :
   134	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   135	        = ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   136	            fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val).image Fin.val := by
   137	    ext t
   138	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_image,
   139	      Finset.mem_univ, true_and]
   140	    constructor
   141	    · rintro ⟨ht, hP⟩
   142	      exact ⟨⟨t, ht⟩, hP, rfl⟩
   143	    · rintro ⟨n, hP, rfl⟩
   144	      exact ⟨n.isLt, hP⟩
   145	  have hstep3 :
   146	      ((Finset.range L.q).filter fun t => (t / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val)
   147	        = Finset.Ico (i.val * (L.q / L.m)) (i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m) := by
   148	    ext t
   149	    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_range, Finset.mem_Ico]
   150	    constructor
   151	    · rintro ⟨htq, hP⟩
   152	      have hlt : t / (L.q / L.m) < L.m := by
   153	        rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   154	        omega
   155	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   156	        rwa [Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hlt] at hP
   157	      have hle : t / (L.q / L.m) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ t := Nat.div_mul_le_self t _
   158	      have hupper : t < (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) := by
   159	        rw [← Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos, hdiv]
   160	        omega
   161	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   162	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   163	      rw [hdiv] at hle
   164	      omega
   165	    · rintro ⟨hlo, hhi⟩
   166	      have hexp : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m)
   167	          = i.val * (L.q / L.m) + L.q / L.m := by ring
   168	      have hdiv : t / (L.q / L.m) = i.val := by
   169	        have h1 : i.val ≤ t / (L.q / L.m) := (Nat.le_div_iff_mul_le hkpos).mpr hlo
   170	        have h2 : t / (L.q / L.m) < i.val + 1 := by
   171	          rw [Nat.div_lt_iff_lt_mul hkpos]
   172	          omega
   173	        omega
   174	      refine ⟨?_, ?_⟩
   175	      · have hbound : (i.val + 1) * (L.q / L.m) ≤ L.m * (L.q / L.m) :=
   176	          Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ i.isLt
   177	        omega
   178	      · rw [hdiv, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt i.isLt]
   179	  rw [hstep1, ← Finset.card_image_of_injective
   180	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (Fin L.q)).filter
   181	        fun n => (n.val / (L.q / L.m)) % L.m = i.val) Fin.val_injective,
   182	    ← hstep2, hstep3, Nat.card_Ico]
   183	  omega

   204	/-- `lem:alnf`: the point and axis-index marginals of the axis line-point

   212	  constructor
   213	  · have hmap : (aLinePointDist L).map Prod.snd
   214	        = (uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.point := by

   217	          fun s => (aLineDescOf L s.1, LdSpace.point s.2)).map Prod.snd) = _
   218	      rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]

   220	    rw [hmap, map_uniformDistribution_point]
   221	  · have hmap : (aLinePointDist L).map (fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed)
   222	        = ((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map LdSpace.seed).map (chiIndex L) := by
   223	      change ((((uniformDistribution (LdSpace L)).map
   224	          fun z => (ldALineCL L z, ldPointCL L z)).map
   225	          fun s => (aLineDescOf L s.1, LdSpace.point s.2)).map
   226	          fun sample => chiIndex L sample.1.seed) = _
   227	      rw [Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map, Distribution.map_map]
   228	      rfl
   229	    rw [hmap, map_uniformDistribution_seed, map_uniformDistribution_chiIndex]

   231	/-- The incidence conclusion of `lem:alnf`, blueprint
   232	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:101-106`, paper
   233	`08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:243-257`. -/
   234	theorem aLinePointDist_mem_line (L : LdParams) :
   235	    ∀ sample ∈ (aLinePointDist L).support, sample.2 ∈ sample.1.pointSet := by
   236	  intro sample hsample
   237	  have hsupport : (aLinePointDist L).support =
   238	      ((Finset.univ : Finset (LdSpace L)).image
   239	        fun z => (ldALineCL L z, ldPointCL L z)).image
   240	        fun s => (aLineDescOf L s.1, LdSpace.point s.2) := rfl
   241	  rw [hsupport] at hsample
   242	  obtain ⟨s, hs, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hsample
   243	  obtain ⟨z, -, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hs
   244	  change LdSpace.point z ∈
   245	    linePoints
   246	      (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)))
   247	        (lineRepMap (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)))
   248	          (LdSpace.point z)))
   249	      (coordinateDirection (chiIndex L (LdSpace.seed z)))
   250	  rw [lineRepMap_apply_self]
   251	  exact mem_linePoints_lineRepMap _ _

    30	/-- The numerical admissible Pauli-test parameter package.  Its scalar carrier
    31	uses the once-and-for-all model `fixedFieldModel q hq`, so the paper's fixed
    32	self-dual-normal identification is not quantified in the test statement.  This
    33	is `def:admissible` in
    34	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    35	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    36	-/
    37	structure AdmissibleParams where
    38	  q : ℕ
    39	  m : ℕ
    40	  d : ℕ
    41	  hd : 1 ≤ d
    42	  hq : IsAdmissibleSize q
    43	  hdvd : m ∣ q
    44	
    45	/-- The positivity of the ambient dimension is a proof obligation implicit in
    46	the admissibility convention `def:admissible`, blueprint
    47	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`, paper origin
    48	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.

    50	theorem AdmissibleParams.one_le_m (P : AdmissibleParams) : 1 ≤ P.m := by
    51	  obtain ⟨k, -, hk⟩ := P.hq
    52	  have hq : 0 < P.q := by
    53	    rw [hk]
    54	    positivity
    55	  exact Nat.pos_of_dvd_of_pos P.hdvd hq

    57	/-- The fixed model accessor for an admissible parameter package.  It is a
    58	compatibility view of the global `fixedFieldModel` selector, not an independently
    59	quantified field representation.  Blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:269-283`; paper
    60	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:958-961`.
    61	-/
    62	noncomputable def AdmissibleParams.model (P : AdmissibleParams) : FixedFieldModel P.q :=
    63	  fixedFieldModel P.q P.hq

    65	/-- The low-degree parameter view of an admissible Pauli-test package.  This is
    66	a Lean-only bridge supporting the statement closure; it is not an additional

    71	def AdmissibleParams.toLdParams (P : AdmissibleParams) : LdParams where
    72	  q := P.q
    73	  m := P.m
    74	  d := P.d
    75	  k := 1
    76	  hm := P.one_le_m
    77	  hd := P.hd
    78	  hk := by decide

    94	inductive PauliType where

    98	  | pauli (W : PauliKind)

   334	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a linear map of coefficient vectors
   335	along an injective reindexing of registers; see `clExtend`.  Supports

   338	private def clReindexLinear {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] {f : κ → ι}
   339	    (hf : Function.Injective f) (L : (κ → K) →ₗ[K] (κ → K)) :
   340	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   341	  toFun x := clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))
   342	  map_add' x y := by
   343	    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (x + y) (f k))) =
   344	      clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k))) + clExtend f (L (fun k => y (f k)))
   345	    have h : (fun k => (x + y) (f k)) =
   346	        (fun k => x (f k)) + (fun k => y (f k)) := rfl
   347	    rw [h, map_add, clExtend_add hf]
   348	  map_smul' c x := by
   349	    show clExtend f (L (fun k => (c • x) (f k))) =
   350	      c • clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))

   354	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: transport a conditionally linear syntax tree

   358	private def clReindexTerm {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ]
   359	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι} (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   360	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell
   361	  | _, .zero => .zero
   362	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ h rest =>
   363	      .succ (S₁.image f) (clReindexLinear hf L₁)
   364	        (by
   365	          intro x i hi
   366	          by_cases hex : ∃ k, f k = i
   367	          · obtain ⟨k, rfl⟩ := hex
   368	            have hk : k ∉ S₁ := fun hk => hi (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk)
   369	            show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) (f k) = 0
   370	            rw [clExtend_apply hf]
   371	            exact h _ k hk
   372	          · show clExtend f (L₁ (fun j => x (f j))) i = 0
   373	            simp [clExtend, Function.extend_apply' _ _ _ hex])
   374	        (fun y => clReindexTerm hf (rest (fun k => y (f k))))

   376	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the transported syntax tree is supported on
   377	any register containing the image of the original support. -/
   378	private theorem clReindexTerm_supportedOn {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   379	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   380	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   381	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (S : Finset κ)
   382	      (T : Finset ι), t.supportedOn S → S.image f ⊆ T →
   383	      (clReindexTerm hf t).supportedOn T := by
   384	  intro ell t
   385	  induction t with
   386	  | zero => intro S T _ _; trivial
   387	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   388	      intro S T hsupp hST
   389	      obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hsupp
   390	      refine ⟨fun i hi => hST (Finset.image_subset_image h1 hi), fun y => ?_⟩
   391	      refine ih (fun k => y (f k)) (S \ S₁) (T \ S₁.image f) (h2 _) ?_
   392	      intro i hi
   393	      obtain ⟨k, hk, rfl⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hi
   394	      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
   395	      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩
   396	      intro hmem
   397	      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   398	      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

   400	/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: evaluation commutes with the transport of a
   401	conditionally linear syntax tree along an injective reindexing. -/
   402	private theorem clReindexTerm_eval {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
   403	    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
   404	    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
   405	    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (x : ι → K),
   406	      CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf t) x =
   407	        clExtend f (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun k => x (f k))) := by
   408	  intro ell t
   409	  induction t with
   410	  | zero => intro x; exact (clExtend_zero hf).symm
   411	  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
   412	      intro x
   413	      have hres : (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k)) =
   414	          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by
   415	        funext k
   416	        by_cases hk : k ∈ S₁
   417	        · have hmem : f k ∈ S₁.image f := Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk
   418	          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hmem]
   419	        · have hni : f k ∉ S₁.image f := by
   420	            intro hmem
   421	            obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
   422	            exact hk (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')
   423	          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hni]
   424	      have hhead : clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) =
   425	          clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))) := by
   426	        show clExtend f (L₁ (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k))) = _
   427	        rw [hres]
   428	      have hcomp : (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
   429	            (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)) =
   430	          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by
   431	        rw [hhead]
   432	        exact clExtend_comp hf _
   433	      show clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) +
   434	          CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf (rest
   435	            (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
   436	              (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)))) x =

   438	          CondLinearTerm.eval
   439	            (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))))
   440	            (fun k => x (f k)))
   441	      rw [hcomp, ih _ x, hhead, ← clExtend_add hf]

  1073	\paragraph{Conditional linear functions for the Pauli basis test.}
  1074	The CL functions corresponding to the Pauli basis test question distribution are
  1075	parameterized by the parameter tuple $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$.
  1076	Let $V^\pauli$ denote the linear space $(\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m
  1077	\times (\F_q)^2$.
  1078	The space $V^\pauli$ is decomposed into a direct sum of the following register
  1079	subspaces: $V_\xpt,V_\zpt$ (which are $m$-dimensional), $V_\coord$ (which is
  1080	$1$-dimensional), $V_{\dir{}}$ (which is $m$-dimensional), and
  1081	$V_{\rxpt},V_{\rzpt}$ (which are $1$-dimensional).
  1082	We identify elements of $V^\pauli$ as tuples $(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1083	\in (\F_q^m)^2 \times \F_q \times \F_q^m \times (\F_q)^2$.
  1084	We define CL functions $L_\tvar: V^\pauli \to V^\pauli$ for every type $\tvar
  1085	\in \type^\pauli$:
  1086	\begin{enumerate}
  1087	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Point,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1088	  = L_\Point(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\Point$ is the $1$-level CL function defined in
  1089	  \Cref{eq:cl-ptf}.\footnote{The range $V_{\xpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus
  1090	    V_{\dir{}}$ or $V_{\zpt} \oplus V_\coord \oplus V_{\dir{}}$ of $L_\Point$ is
  1091	    embedded in $V^\pauli$ in the natural way.
  1092	    The same convention is used also in Item 2 and 3 for $L_\ALine$ and
  1093	    $L_\DLine$.}
  1094	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\ALine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1095	  = L_\ALine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\ALine$ is the $2$-level CL function defined in
  1096	  \Cref{eq:cl-alnf}.
  1097	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\DLine,W}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)
  1098	  = L_\DLine(u_W,s,v)$ where $L_\DLine$ is the $3$-level CL function defined in
  1099	  \Cref{eq:cl-dlnf}.
  1100	\item For $\tvar \in \type^\ms \cup \{\Pair, (\Pair,X), (\Pair,Z) \}$,
  1101	  $L_{\tvar}(u_\xpt,u_\zpt,s,v,r_\xpt,r_\zpt) =
  1102	  (u_\xpt,u_\zpt,0,0,r_\xpt,r_\zpt)$, i.e., it projects onto $V_\xpt \oplus
  1103	  V_\zpt \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$.
  1104	  Thus $L_{\tvar}$ is a $1$-level CL function.
  1105	  
  1106	\item For $W \in \{X,Z\}$, define $L_{\Pauli,W} = 0$ as the identically $0$
  1107	  function.
  1108	  Thus it is a $0$-level CL function.
  1109	
  1110	\end{enumerate}
  1111	We note that the maps $L_{\Point,W}, L_{\ALine,W}, L_{\DLine,W}$ act as the zero function
  1112	on $V_{\overline{W}} \oplus V_{\rxpt} \oplus V_{\rzpt}$ where $\overline{W} = X$
  1113	if $W = Z$ and $\overline{W} = Z$ if $W = X$.
  1114	
  1115	The question distribution of $\game^\pauli$ is thus a typed CL distribution on

  1119	in Figure~\ref{fig:type-graph-pauli}, sampling a uniformly random $z \in
  1120	V^\pauli$, and then setting $x_w = L_{\tvar_w}(z)$ for $w \in \AB$.

    11	Intuitively, a conditionally linear function takes as input an element
    12	$x\in V = \F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$, and applies linear maps $L_j$ sequentially
    13	on $x^{V_j}$ where $V_1,V_2,\ldots $ are a sequence of complementary register
    14	subspaces such that both the linear maps $L_j$ and the subspace $V_j$ for
    15	$j \ge 2$ may depend on the values taken by previous linear maps $L_1(x^{V_1})$,
    16	$L_2(x^{V_2})$, etc.
    17	
    18	In the remainder of the section we use $V$ to denote the linear space $\F^n$ for
    19	some integer $n \geq 0$.
    20	For ease of notation we extensively use the subscript range notation.
    21	For example, if $V_1, V_2, \ldots, V_\ell$ are fixed subspaces of $V$ and $k \in
    22	\{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ we write
    23	\begin{equation*}
    24	  V_{<k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\,1 \le j<k} V_j\;,\quad
    25	  V_{> k} = \bigoplus_{j\,:\, \ell\ge j > k} V_j\;,
    26	\end{equation*}
    27	and it is understood that $V_{\le k}$ and $V_{\ge k}$ are identical to
    28	$V_{<k+1}$ and $V_{>k-1}$, respectively.
    29	Moreover, if $V'$ is a register subspace of $V$, $F: V' \to V'$ is a function,
    30	and $x \in V$, we write $x^F$ to denote $F(x^{V'})$.
    31	For example, in the following definition $x^{L_1}$ is used as shorthand notation
    32	for $L_1(x^{V_1})$.
    33	
    34	
    35	\begin{definition}
    36	  \label{def:cl-func}
    37		Let $V$ be $\F^n$ for some $n\geq 0$.
    38	  For all integers $\ell\geq 0$ the collection of \emph{$\ell$-level
    39	    conditionally linear functions} (implicitly, \emph{on $V$}) is defined
    40	  inductively as follows.
    41	  \begin{enumerate}
    42	  \item There is a single $0$-level conditionally linear function, which is the
    43	    $0$ function on $V$.
    44	
    45	  \item Let $\ell \geq 1$ and suppose the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level
    46	    conditionally linear functions has been defined.
    47	    The collection of $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions on $V$ consists
    48	    of all functions $L$ on $V$ that can be expressed in the following form.
    49	    There exist complementary register subspaces $V_1$ and $V_{>1}$ of $V$, a
    50	    linear function $L_1$ on $V_1$, and for all $v \in L_1(V_1)$, an
    51	    $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear function $L_{>1,\, v}$ on $V_{>1}$,
    52	    such that for all $x\in V$,
    53	    \begin{equation*}
    54	      L(x) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}} (x^{V_{>1}})\;.
    55	    \end{equation*}
    56	  \end{enumerate}
    57	\end{definition}
    58	
    59	The concept of conditionally linear functions is simple even though the
    60	notations seem complicated.
    61	It is best understood using an operational definition illustrated in
    62	\cref{fig:cl-functions}.
    63	We give an example of a $2$-level CL function in \cref{ex:cl-function}.
    64	
    65	\begin{remark}
    66	  \label{rk:level-1-is-linear}
    67	  It follows from the above definition that all $1$-level CL functions are linear.
    68	\end{remark}
    69	
    70	\begin{example}\label{ex:cl-function}
    71	Consider $V = \F_{2}^{3}$. Then the following map
    72	\begin{equation*}
    73	  L:(x_{0}, x_{1}, x_{2})
    74	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0},  x_{2})
    75	\end{equation*}
    76	on $V$ is a $2$-level CL function by choosing $V_{1} = \mathrm{span}\{(0,0,1)\}$, $L_{1}$
    77	the identity function on $V_{1}$, $V_{2} = V_{1}^{\perp}$, and
    78	\begin{equation*}
    79	  L_{2,\, x_{2}}: (x_{0}, x_{1}, 0)
    80	  \mapsto (0, x_{0}x_{2} + x_{1}x_{2} + x_{0}, 0),
    81	\end{equation*}
    82	which is linear for all $x_{2} \in \F_{2}$.
    83	Note that intuitively the function $L$ selects either $x_{0}$ or $x_{1}$ in the
    84	second coordinate conditioning on the value of $x_{2}$.
    85	\end{example}

   122	\begin{remark}
   123	  \label{rk:higher-level}
   124	  Note that for any integer $\ell\geq 1$ the collection of $\ell$-level CL
   125	  functions trivially contains the collection of $(\ell-1)$-level CL functions:
   126	  for this it suffices to note that the $0$ function, which is a $0$-level CL
   127	  function, is also a $1$-level CL function by setting $V_1=V$, $V_{>1}= \{0\}$,
   128	  $L_1(x)=0$ for all $x\in V$, and $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is the $0$ map for all
   129	  $x\in V$.
   130	\end{remark}

   132	\begin{definition}
   133	  \label{def:cl-dist}
   134	  Let $L, R: V \to V$ be conditionally linear functions.
   135	  The \emph{conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ corresponding to $(L,
   136	    R)$} is defined as the distribution over pairs $(L(x), R(x)) \in V \times V$
   137	  for $x$ drawn uniformly at random from $V$.
   138	\end{definition}
   139	
   140	Throughout the paper we abbreviate ``conditionally linear functions'' and
   141	``conditionally linear distributions'' as \emph{CL functions} and \emph{CL
   142	  distributions}, respectively.
   143	
   144	The following lemma elucidates structural properties of $\ell$-level CL
   145	functions.
   146	Recall that using our shorthand notation, $x^{L_{<k}}$ and $x^{L_k}$ in the
   147	lemma denote $L_{<k}(x)$ and $L_{k,u}(x^{V_{k,\, u}})$ where $u = L_{<k}(x)$.
   148	
   149	
   150	\begin{lemma}
   151	  \label{lem:cl-kth}
   152		Let $\ell \geq 1$ and $V = \F^n$ for some integer $n \geq 0$.
   153	  A function $L: V \to V$ is an $\ell$-level CL function if and only if the
   154	  following collection of functions and subspaces exists:
   155	  \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
   156	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-marginal} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$, a
   157	    function $L_{\le k} : V \to V$ called the \emph{$k$-th marginal of $L$};
   158	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-space} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u
   159	    \in L_{<k} (V)$, a register subspace $V_{k,\, u}$ of $V$ called the
   160	    \emph{$k$-th factor space with prefix $u$};
   161	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-map} For each $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, \ell\}$ and $u \in
   162	    L_{<k} (V)$, a linear map $L_{k,\, u} : V_{k,\, u} \to V_{k,\, u}$ called
   163	    the \emph{$k$-th linear map of $L$ with prefix $u$};
   164	  \end{enumerate}
   165	  such that the following conditions hold for all $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots,
   166	  \ell\}$.
   167	  \begin{enumerate}
   168	  \item \label{enu:cl-k-cl} $L_{\leq k}$ is a $k$-level CL function on $V$;
   169		\item \label{enu:cl-space-sum} $V = \bigoplus_{i = 1}^\ell V_{i,\,
   170	      x^{L_{<i}}}$ for all $x \in V$;
   171	\item \label{enu:cl-map-sum} $L_{\leq k}(x) = \sum_{i = 1}^{k} x^{L_i}$ for
   172	    all $x \in V$, where $L_i$ is shorthand notation for $L_{i,\,
   173	      x^{L_{<i}}}$;
   174	  \item \label{enu:cl-last-ell} $L = L_{\leq \ell}$.
   175	  \end{enumerate}
   176	  As in \cref{enu:cl-map-sum}, we sometimes use $V_k$ and $L_k$ to denote
   177	  $V_{k,\, u}$ and $L_{k,\, u}$ respectively, leaving the prefix $u$ implicit.
   178	\end{lemma}
   179	
   180	\begin{proof}
   181		We first prove the ``if'' direction: if there exist spaces and functions
   182	  satisfying the conditions in the lemma, the fact that $L$ is an $\ell$-level
   183	  CL function follows from \cref{enu:cl-k-cl,enu:cl-last-ell} of the lemma
   184	  statement.
   185	
   186	  We now prove the ``only if'' direction.
   187	  Given a CL function $L$ on $V$, we construct the $k$-th family of subspaces
   188	  and functions for all $k \in \{1, \ldots, \ell\}$ by induction on the level
   189	  $\ell$.
   190	  First consider the base case $\ell=1$.
   270	  $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ by the inductive hypothesis.
   271	  This shows that $L_{\le k}$, $V_{k,\, u}$, and $L_{k,\, u}$ satisfy the
   272	  conditions of the lemma and completes the induction.
   273	\end{proof}
   274	
   275	We note that the marginal functions, factor spaces, and linear maps of a given
   276	CL function $L$ may not be unique; for example, consider the identity function
   277	on a linear space $V = \F^n$.
   278	This is clearly a $1$-level CL function, but it can also be viewed as a
   279	$k$-level CL function for $k \in \{2, \ldots, n\}$ with an arbitrary partition
   280	of $V$ into factor spaces.

   282	\begin{lemma}
   283	  \label{lem:cl-concat}
   284	  Let $\ell, k \ge 0$ be integers and $U = \F^n$, $V = \F^m$ be linear spaces.
   285	  Suppose $L$ is a $k$-level CL function on $U$ and $R_u$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   286	  function on $V$ for each $u \in L(U)$.
   287	  Then the \emph{concatenation} $T$ of $L$ and $\{R_u\}_u$ defined as
   288	  \begin{equation*}
   289	    T (x) = L(x^U) + R_{L(x^U)} (x^V)
   290	  \end{equation*}
   291	  is a $(k+\ell)$-level conditionally linear function on $U\oplus V$.
   292	\end{lemma}
   293	
   294	\begin{proof}
   295	  We prove the claim by induction on $k$.
   296	  The case $k = 0$ follows from the Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   297	  Assume that the lemma holds for $L$ being at most $(k-1)$-level.
   298	  By Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}, there are complementary register subspaces
   299	  $U_1$ and $U_{>1}$ of $U$, a linear function $L_1$ on $U_1$, and a family of
   300	  $(k-1)$-level CL functions $L_{>1,\, v}$ for $v \in L_1(U_1)$ such that
   301	  \begin{equation*}
   302	    L(x^U) = x^{L_1} + L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}).
   303	  \end{equation*}
   304	  For all $x^{L_1}$, define the function $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ on $U_{>1} \oplus V$ as
   305	  \begin{equation*}
   306	    T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1} \oplus V}) = L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}(x^{U_{>1}}) +
   307	    R_{x^{L_1} + x^{L_{>1}}}(x^V),
   308	  \end{equation*}
   309	  the concatenation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ and $\{ R_{L(x^U)} \}_{x^{L_{>1}}}$
   310	  where $L_{>1}$ is the shorthand notation of $L_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$.
   311	  By the induction hypothesis, $T_{>1,\, x^{L_1}}$ is $(k+\ell-1)$-level
   312	  conditionally linear.
   313	  The lemma follows from Definition~\ref{def:cl-func}.
   314	\end{proof}
   315	\begin{lemma}[Direct sums of CL functions]
   316	  \label{lem:cl-func-prod}
   317	  Let $V^{(1)}, V^{(2)}, \ldots, V^{(m)}$ be register subspaces of $V$ such that
   318	  $V = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   319	  Suppose that, for each $j\in\{1, 2, \ldots, m\}$, $L^{(j)}$ is an
   320	  $\ell_j$-level conditionally linear function on $V^{(j)}$.
   321	  Then the direct sum $L = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}$ is an $\ell$-level CL
   322	  function over $V$ for $\ell = \max_j \{\ell_j\}$, where $L$ is defined by
   323	  \begin{equation*}
   324	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m  L^{(j)}(x^{(j)})
   325	  \end{equation*}
   326	  for all $x = \sum_{j=1}^m x^{(j)} \in \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}$.
   327	\end{lemma}
   328	
   329	\begin{proof}
   330	  It is easy to see that an $\ell$-level CL function is also $k$-level
   331	  conditionally linear for all $k \ge \ell$.
   332	  Hence, it suffices to prove the claim where $\ell_j = \ell$ for $j=1, 2,
   333	  \ldots, m$.
   334	
   335	  We prove the theorem by an induction on $\ell$.
   336	  For $\ell = 1$, the functions $L^{(j)}$ are linear and the claim follows by
   337	  the fact that the direct sum of linear maps is linear.
   338	
   339	  Assume now the theorem holds for conditionally linear functions of level at
   340	  most $\ell-1$ and $L^{(j)}$ are $\ell$-level conditionally linear functions
   341	  for $j=1, 2, ,\ldots, m$.
   342	  By definition, $L^{(j)}$ is the concatenation of conditionally linear
   343	  functions $L^{(j)}_{1}$ on $V^{(j)}_1$ and $\{ L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j} \}_{v_j}$
   344	  on $V^{(j)}_{>1}$ of levels $1$, and $\ell-1$ respectively.
   345	  Furthermore,
   346	  \begin{equation*}
   347	    L(x) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)} (x^{(j)}) = \sum_{j=1}^m \Bigl( v_j +
   348	    L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   349	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr) \Bigr),
   350	  \end{equation*}
   351	  where $v_j = L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   352	    \Bigr)$.
   353	  By the induction hypothesis,
   354	  \begin{equation*}
   355	    L_{1} (x^{V_1}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{1}\Bigl( (x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_1}
   356	    \Bigr),\quad L_{>1,\, v} (x^{V_{>1}}) = \sum_{j=1}^m L^{(j)}_{>1,\, v_j}
   357	    \Bigl((x^{(j)})^{V^{(j)}_{>1}} \Bigr)
   358	  \end{equation*}
   359	  are $1$-level and $(\ell-1)$-level conditionally linear respectively for $v =
   360	  \sum_j v_j$, $V_1 = \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_1$, and $V_{>1} =
   361	  \bigoplus_{j=1}^m V^{(j)}_{>1}$.
   362	  This proves that $L$ is $\ell$-level conditionally linear.
   363	\end{proof}
   364	
   365	\begin{lemma}
   366	  \label{lem:cl-dist-prod}
   367	  For each $i \in \{1,\ldots,m\}$ let $L^{(i)}, R^{(i)} : V^{(i)} \to V^{(i)}$
   368	  be $\ell_i$-level conditionally linear functions and let $L, R: V \to V$ be the
   369	  direct sums $L = \bigoplus_i L_i$ and $R = \bigoplus_i R_i$, respectively, as
   370	  defined in Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}.
   371	  Then the conditionally linear distribution $\mu_{L, R}$ is the product
   372	  distribution $\prod_{i=1}^m \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ over $V \times V$.
   373	\end{lemma}
   374	
   375	\begin{proof}
   376		The distribution $\mu_{L,R}$ is the distribution over pairs $(L(x),R(x))$
   377	  where $x$ is sampled uniformly from $V \times V$.
   378	  By Lemma~\ref{lem:cl-func-prod}, this is equivalent to the distribution over
   379	  pairs $\bigl( (L_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m, (R_i(x^{V_i}))_{i=1}^m \bigr)$ where $x$
   380	  is chosen uniformly at random from $V$.
   381	  This distribution is exactly the product of the distributions $
   382	  \mu_{L^{(i)},\, R^{(i)}}$ for $i = 1, 2, \ldots, m$.
   383	\end{proof}

   108	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {S S₁ : Finset ι} {ell : ℕ}
   109	    (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   110	    (hS₁ : S₁ ⊆ S) (hSupport : ∀ x a, a ∉ S₁ → L₁ x a = 0)
   111	    (R : (ι → K) → (ι → K) → (ι → K))
   112	    (hR : ∀ y, IsCondLinearOn K (S \ S₁) ell (R y)) :

   115	        R (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x)) x) := by
   116	  classical
   117	  choose t ht ht_eval using hR
   118	  refine ⟨.succ S₁ L₁ hSupport t, ⟨hS₁, ht⟩, ?_⟩
   119	  funext x
   120	  change L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x) +
   121	      CondLinearTerm.eval (t (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ x))) x = _

   150	private def coordinateRestrictionLinear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   151	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) :
   152	    (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K) where
   153	  toFun := coordinateRestriction S
   154	  map_add' := coordinateRestriction_add S

   159	private theorem sum_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   160	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   161	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   162	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (x : ι → K) :
   163	    ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x = x := by
   164	  classical
   165	  ext a
   166	  obtain ⟨j, haj⟩ := hCover a
   167	  rw [Finset.sum_apply, Finset.sum_eq_single j]
   168	  · simp [coordinateRestriction, haj]
   169	  · intro i _ hij
   170	    have hai : a ∉ V i := fun hai =>
   171	      Finset.disjoint_left.mp (hDisjoint i j hij) hai haj
   172	    simp [coordinateRestriction, hai]
   173	  · exact fun hj => (hj (Finset.mem_univ j)).elim
   174	
   175	private theorem sum_eq_iff_coordinateRestriction_eq {K ι J : Type*} [Field K]
   176	    [DecidableEq ι] [Fintype J]
   177	    (V : J → Finset ι) (hDisjoint : ∀ i j, i ≠ j → Disjoint (V i) (V j))
   178	    (hCover : ∀ a, ∃ j, a ∈ V j) (f : J → ι → K)
   179	    (hf : ∀ j a, a ∉ V j → f j a = 0) (x : ι → K) :
   180	    (∑ j, f j) = x ↔ ∀ j, f j = coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   181	  classical
   182	  constructor
   183	  · intro h j
   184	    rw [← h]
   185	    exact (coordinateRestriction_sum_eq V hDisjoint f hf j).symm
   186	  · intro h
   187	    calc
   188	      (∑ j, f j) = ∑ j, coordinateRestriction (V j) x := by
   189	        exact Finset.sum_congr rfl fun j _ => h j
   190	      _ = x := sum_coordinateRestriction_eq V hDisjoint hCover x

   192	/-- The value of the strict-prefix marginal preceding `k`. This is a
   193	formalization-only auxiliary for `lem:cl-kth`, blueprint
   194	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1074-1094`, paper
   195	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
   196	def clPrefix {K ι : Type*} [Zero K] {ell : ℕ}
   197	    (marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) (k : Fin ell)
   198	    (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
   199	  if _hk : k.val = 0 then 0
   200	  else marginal ⟨k.val - 1, lt_of_le_of_lt (Nat.sub_le _ _) k.isLt⟩ x
   201	
   202	/-- Prefix-indexed decomposition data from `lem:cl-kth`. Factor spaces are
   203	represented by their coordinate sets, matching the register-subspace encoding
   204	used by `IsCondLinearOn`. Blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1074-1094`, paper
   205	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:150-178`. -/
   206	structure CLData (K ι : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
   207	    (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
   208	  /-- The marginal `L_{≤k}`. -/
   209	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
   210	  /-- The factor register selected by a prefix value. -/
   211	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
   212	  /-- The linear map selected by a prefix value. -/
   213	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   214	  /-- Each marginal has the corresponding conditionally linear level. -/
   215	  marginal_cl : ∀ k, IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ (k.val + 1) (marginal k)
   216	  /-- The selected factor registers are pairwise disjoint. -/
   217	  factor_disjoint : ∀ x i j, i ≠ j →
   218	    Disjoint (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) (factor j (clPrefix marginal j x))
   219	  /-- The selected factor registers cover all coordinates. -/
   220	  factor_cover : ∀ x a, ∃ i, a ∈ factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   221	  /-- Each selected linear map is supported on its factor register. -/
   222	  linear_supported : ∀ k u x a, a ∉ factor k u → linear k u x a = 0
   223	  /-- Each marginal is the sum of the preceding selected linear pieces. -/
   224	  sum_formula : ∀ k x, marginal k x =
   225	    ∑ i : Fin ell, if i.val ≤ k.val then
   226	      linear i (clPrefix marginal i x)
   227	        (coordinateRestriction (factor i (clPrefix marginal i x)) x) else 0
   228	  /-- The final marginal is the original function. -/
   229	  top : ∀ h : 0 < ell,
   230	    marginal ⟨ell - 1, Nat.sub_lt h (by decide)⟩ = L
   231	
   232	/-- Prefix decomposition data on a register `S`, refining the decomposition
   233	in `lem:cl-kth`. -/
   234	private structure CLDataOn (K ι : Type*) [Field K] [Fintype ι]
   235	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
   236	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) where
   237	  marginal : Fin ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
   238	  factor : Fin ell → (ι → K) → Finset ι
   239	  linear : Fin ell → (ι → K) → ((ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
   240	  marginal_cl : ∀ k, IsCondLinearOn K S (k.val + 1) (marginal k)

     3	/-!
     4	# Conditionally linear functions and graph distributions
     5	
     6	The question distributions in the Pauli basis test are generated by a finite
     7	graph of types and a shared seed, with each type applying a conditionally linear
     8	map to that seed.  The inductive predicate below records the level structure
     9	needed by later formalization stages.  The coordinate direct-sum development
    10	built on that predicate lives in
    11	`MIPStarRE/QPBT/Games/CondLinearTheorems/DirectSumSupport.lean`.
    12	
    13	## References
    14	
    15	The source-facing nodes are `def:cl-func`, `def:cl-dist`, `lem:cl-concat`, and
    16	`def:graph-distribution` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1257`.
    17	The paper origins are
    18	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57,282-314`
    19	and `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1010`.
    20	-/
    21	
    22	open scoped BigOperators
    23	
    24	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    25	
    26	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    27	
    28	variable {K ι : Type*} [Field K] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    29	
    30	/--
    31	The source definition is recursive in the residual map.  A direct inductive
    32	predicate with that recursive occurrence under a dependent finite-set index is
    33	rejected by Lean's strict-positivity checker.  We therefore expose the same
    34	public predicate through a positive syntax tree (`CondLinearTerm`), together
    35	with its support invariant and evaluation function.  This is a representation
    36	deviation forced by Lean, not an additional mathematical hypothesis.  It encodes
    37	`def:cl-func`, blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`,
    38	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    39	-/
    40	inductive CondLinearTerm (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    41	    [DecidableEq ι] : ℕ → Type _ where
    42	  | zero : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) 0
    43	  | succ {ell : ℕ}
    44	      (S₁ : Finset ι)
    45	      (L₁ : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K))
    46	      (hSupport : ∀ x i, i ∉ S₁ → L₁ x i = 0)
    47	      (rest : (ι → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell) :
    48	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) (ell + 1)
    49	
    50	/-- Restrict a coordinate vector to a register, zeroing the complementary
    51	coordinates.  This is Lean-only support for the projections in `def:cl-func`,
    52	blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    53	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    54	-/
    55	def coordinateRestriction (S : Finset ι) (x : ι → K) : ι → K :=
    56	  fun i => if i ∈ S then x i else 0
    57	
    58	/-- Evaluation of a representation of a conditionally linear function.
    59	Lean-only support for `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    60	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    61	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    62	-/
    63	def CondLinearTerm.eval {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    64	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    65	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → (ι → K) → (ι → K)
    66	  | _, .zero => fun _ => 0
    67	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ _ rest =>
    68	      fun x =>
    69	        let x₁ := coordinateRestriction S₁ x
    70	        L₁ x₁ + CondLinearTerm.eval (rest (L₁ x₁)) x
    71	
    72	/-- The support invariant for a representation of a conditionally linear
    73	function.  This is a Lean-only companion to `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    74	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    75	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    76	-/
    77	def CondLinearTerm.supportedOn {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    78	    {K : Type*} [Field K] :
    79	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell → Finset ι → Prop
    80	  | _, .zero, _ => True
    81	  | _, .succ S₁ _ _ rest, S =>
    82	      S₁ ⊆ S ∧ ∀ y, CondLinearTerm.supportedOn (rest y) (S \ S₁)
    83	
    84	/-- The public conditionally-linear predicate.  Its positive syntax-tree
    85	encoding is the Lean representation of `def:cl-func`, blueprint
    86	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`, paper origin
    87	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    88	-/
    89	def IsCondLinearOn (K : Type*) [Field K] {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    90	    [DecidableEq ι] (S : Finset ι) (ell : ℕ)
    91	    (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    92	  ∃ t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell,
    93	    CondLinearTerm.supportedOn t S ∧ CondLinearTerm.eval t = L
    94	
    95	/--
    96	`IsCondLinear` abbreviates the full-coordinate predicate.  Blueprint
    97	`def:cl-func`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:1053-1063`; paper
    98	`references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`.
    99	-/
   100	def IsCondLinear (ell : ℕ) (L : (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
   101	  IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L

   103	/-- The zero conditionally linear function at every level, used to extend the
   104	family `R u` from the image `L(U)` to all indices in the concatenation

   108	  | 0 => .zero
   109	  | ell + 1 => .succ ∅ 0 (by simp) (fun _ => zeroOfLevel ell)

   114	    CondLinearTerm.eval (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) x = 0 := by
   115	  induction ell with
   116	  | zero => rfl
   117	  | succ ell ih =>

   123	      (CondLinearTerm.zeroOfLevel (K := K) (ι := ι) ell) S := by

   129	/-- Extending the support set preserves the support invariant. -/
   130	private theorem CondLinearTerm.supportedOn_mono {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
   131	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {ell : ℕ}
   132	    {t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := ι) ell} {S T : Finset ι}

   136	  | zero => trivial

   138	      rcases ht with ⟨hS₁, hrest⟩
   139	      refine ⟨hS₁.trans hST, fun y => ih y (hrest y) ?_⟩

   142	/-- Lift a linear map to the left summand of a direct sum of registers. -/

   148	    ext i
   149	    cases i with
   150	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   151	    | inr i => simp
   152	  map_smul' c x := by
   153	    ext i
   154	    cases i with
   155	    | inl i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i
   156	    | inr i => simp

   161	    (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) →ₗ[K] (ιU ⊕ ιV → K) where
   162	  toFun x := Sum.elim 0 (L (fun i => x (.inr i)))
   163	  map_add' x y := by
   164	    ext i
   165	    cases i with
   166	    | inl i => simp
   167	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_add _ _) i
   168	  map_smul' c x := by
   169	    ext i
   170	    cases i with
   171	    | inl i => simp
   172	    | inr i => exact congrFun (L.map_smul c _) i

   174	/-- Lift a representation of a conditionally linear function to the right
   175	summand of a direct sum of registers. -/
   176	private def CondLinearTerm.liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   177	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV] :
   178	    {ell : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell →
   179	      CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU ⊕ ιV) ell
   180	  | _, .zero => .zero
   181	  | _, .succ S₁ L₁ hSupport rest =>
   182	      .succ (S₁.map Function.Embedding.inr) (condLinearLiftRight L₁)
   183	        (by
   184	          intro x i hi
   185	          cases i with
   186	          | inl i => rfl
   187	          | inr i =>
   188	              apply hSupport
   189	              simpa using hi)
   190	        (fun y => liftRight (rest (fun i => y (.inr i))))

   193	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_liftRight {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   194	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]

   198	  induction t with
   199	  | zero =>

   202	      ext i

   204	        simp [CondLinearTerm.liftRight, CondLinearTerm.eval, condLinearLiftRight,

   226	/-- Append a family of right-coordinate terms after a left-coordinate term,

   228	private def CondLinearTerm.concat {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   229	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]
   230	    {ell : ℕ} (rTerm : (ιU → K) → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιV) ell)

   232	    {k : ℕ} → CondLinearTerm K (ι := ιU) k →

   238	          intro x i hi
   239	          cases i with
   240	          | inl i =>
   241	              apply hSupport
   242	              simpa using hi
   243	          | inr i => rfl)
   244	        (fun y => concat rTerm (acc + fun i => y (.inl i))

   247	private theorem CondLinearTerm.eval_concat {K ιU ιV : Type*} [Field K]
   248	    [Fintype ιU] [DecidableEq ιU] [Fintype ιV] [DecidableEq ιV]

+/-! ### Push-forwards of finite and uniform distributions
+
+The results of this section are not named in the paper.  They record the
+elementary behaviour of push-forwards of finite distributions, and of uniform
+distributions on finite types, that the line-point samplers of the low-degree
+game and the identification of question distributions with typed conditionally
+linear distributions rely on.
+-/
+
+/-- Two finite distributions coincide as soon as their supports and their
+weight functions coincide.  Formalization-only extensionality principle for
+`Distribution`. -/
+theorem Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight {α : Type*} {μ ν : Distribution α}
+    (hsupport : μ.support = ν.support) (hweight : μ.weight = ν.weight) :
+    μ = ν := by
+  cases μ with
+  | mk s w hn ho =>
+    cases ν with
+    | mk s' w' hn' ho' =>
+      have hs : s = s' := hsupport
+      have hw : w = w' := hweight
+      subst hs
+      subst hw
+      rfl
+
+/-- Successive push-forwards of a finite distribution compose.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.map`. -/
+theorem Distribution.map_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [DecidableEq β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (μ : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → γ) :
+    (μ.map e).map f = μ.map fun a => f (e a) := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (μ.support.image e).image f = μ.support.image fun a => f (e a)
+    rw [Finset.image_image]
+    rfl
+  · funext c
+    have hmaps : ∀ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c,
+        e a ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c := by
+      intro a ha
+      obtain ⟨ha1, ha2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp ha
+      exact Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_image_of_mem _ ha1, ha2⟩
+    have hkey := Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to hmaps μ.weight
+    change (∑ b ∈ (μ.support.image e).filter fun b => f b = c,
+        ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => e a = b, μ.weight a) =
+      ∑ a ∈ μ.support.filter fun a => f (e a) = c, μ.weight a
+    rw [← hkey]
+    refine Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b hb => ?_
+    obtain ⟨-, hb2⟩ := Finset.mem_filter.mp hb
+    congr 1
+    ext a
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter]
+    constructor
+    · rintro ⟨ha1, rfl⟩
+      exact ⟨⟨ha1, hb2⟩, rfl⟩
+    · rintro ⟨⟨ha1, -⟩, hae⟩
+      exact ⟨ha1, hae⟩
+
+/-- Every point of a finite type carries the same uniform weight.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α : Type*)
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α] (a : α) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).weight a = 1 / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
+  simp [uniformDistribution]
+
+/-- A map whose fibers all have the same cardinality pushes the uniform
+distribution forward to the uniform distribution.  Formalization-only
+auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β]
+    (e : α → β) (c : ℕ)
+    (hc : ∀ b : β, ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).card = c) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map e = uniformDistribution β := by
+  have hcpos : 0 < c := by
+    obtain ⟨a₀⟩ := (inferInstance : Nonempty α)
+    have hmem : a₀ ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = e a₀ :=
+      Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩
+    have hpos := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨a₀, hmem⟩
+    rwa [hc] at hpos
+  have hcard : Fintype.card α = Fintype.card β * c := by
+    have h := Finset.card_eq_sum_card_fiberwise
+      (f := e) (s := (Finset.univ : Finset α)) (t := (Finset.univ : Finset β))
+      (fun a _ => Finset.mem_univ _)
+    rw [Finset.card_univ] at h
+    rw [h, Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => hc b]
+    simp [Finset.card_univ, mul_comm]
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).image e = (Finset.univ : Finset β)
+    ext b
+    simp only [Finset.mem_image, Finset.mem_univ, iff_true, true_and]
+    have hne : ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b).Nonempty := by
+      rw [← Finset.card_pos, hc]
+      exact hcpos
+    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hne
+    exact ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩
+  · funext b
+    have hbeta : (Fintype.card β : Error) ≠ 0 := by
+      exact_mod_cast Fintype.card_ne_zero (α := β)
+    have hc' : (c : Error) ≠ 0 := by exact_mod_cast hcpos.ne'
+    change (∑ a ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => e a = b,
+        (uniformDistribution α).weight a) = (uniformDistribution β).weight b
+    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply α a,
+      uniformDistribution_weight_apply, Finset.sum_const, hc, nsmul_eq_mul, hcard]
+    push_cast
+    field_simp
+
+/-- Relabelling along a bijection preserves uniformity.  Formalization-only
+auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_equiv {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] (E : α ≃ β) :
+    (uniformDistribution α).map E = uniformDistribution β := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ 1 fun b => ?_
+  have hfilter :
+      ((Finset.univ : Finset α).filter fun a => E a = b) = {E.symm b} := by
+    ext a
+    simp [Equiv.apply_eq_iff_eq_symm_apply]
+  rw [hfilter]
+  simp
+
+/-- The first marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_fst {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.fst = uniformDistribution α := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card β) fun a => ?_
+  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => p.1 = a)
+      = ({a} : Finset α) ×ˢ (Finset.univ : Finset β) := by
+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
+      Finset.mem_singleton, and_true]
+  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
+  simp
+
+/-- The second marginal of the uniform distribution on a product is uniform.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `uniformDistribution`. -/
+theorem uniformDistribution_map_snd {α β : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] :
+    (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map Prod.snd = uniformDistribution β := by
+  refine uniformDistribution_map_of_card_fiber _ (Fintype.card α) fun b => ?_
+  have hfilter : ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => p.2 = b)
+      = (Finset.univ : Finset α) ×ˢ ({b} : Finset β) := by
+    ext p
+    simp only [Finset.mem_filter, Finset.mem_univ, true_and, Finset.mem_product,
+      Finset.mem_singleton]
+  rw [hfilter, Finset.card_product]
+  simp
+
+/-- Binding a uniform distribution to a family of uniformly seeded
+push-forwards is the push-forward of the uniform distribution on the product.
+Formalization-only auxiliary for `Distribution.bind`. -/
+theorem bind_uniformDistribution_map {α β γ : Type*}
+    [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
+    [Fintype β] [DecidableEq β] [Nonempty β] [DecidableEq γ]
+    (g : α → β → γ) :
+    Distribution.bind (uniformDistribution α)
+        (fun a => (uniformDistribution β).map (g a)) =
+      (uniformDistribution (α × β)).map fun p => g p.1 p.2 := by
+  refine Distribution.ext_of_support_of_weight ?_ ?_
+  · change (Finset.univ : Finset α).biUnion
+        (fun a => (Finset.univ : Finset β).image (g a)) =
+      (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).image fun p => g p.1 p.2
+    ext c
+    simp [Prod.exists]
+  · funext c
+    have hcount :
+        ((Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c).card
+          = ∑ a : α, ((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card := by
+      simp only [Finset.card_filter]
+      rw [Fintype.sum_prod_type]
+    have hinner : ∀ a : α,
+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
+          = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
+              (1 / (Fintype.card β : Error)) := by
+      intro a
+      change (∑ b ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c,
+          (uniformDistribution β).weight b) = _
+      rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun b _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply β b,
+        Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul]
+    have key : ∀ a : α, (uniformDistribution α).weight a *
+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c
+        = (((Finset.univ : Finset β).filter fun b => g a b = c).card : Error) *
+            (1 / ((Fintype.card α : Error) * (Fintype.card β : Error))) := by
+      intro a
+      rw [uniformDistribution_weight_apply, hinner a]
+      ring
+    change (∑ a ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset α), (uniformDistribution α).weight a *
+        ((uniformDistribution β).map (g a)).weight c) =
+      ∑ p ∈ (Finset.univ : Finset (α × β)).filter fun p => g p.1 p.2 = c,
+        (uniformDistribution (α × β)).weight p
+    rw [Finset.sum_congr rfl fun a _ => key a, ← Finset.sum_mul,
+      Finset.sum_congr rfl fun p _ => uniformDistribution_weight_apply (α × β) p,
+      Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul, hcount, Fintype.card_prod]
+    push_cast
+    ring
+

    52	        ⟨a, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).1, (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2⟩)).elim

    77	theorem map_sum_smul {α β M : Type*} [DecidableEq β]
    78	    [AddCommMonoid M] [Module Error M]
    79	    (𝒟 : Distribution α) (e : α → β) (f : β → M) :

    83	  calc

    89	          intro b _
    90	          rw [Finset.sum_smul]
    91	          refine Finset.sum_congr rfl ?_
    92	          intro a ha
    93	          exact congrArg (fun x => 𝒟.weight a • f x) (Finset.mem_filter.mp ha).2.symm

    96	            (s := 𝒟.support) (t := 𝒟.support.image e) (g := e)

     4	# Uniform subset estimates
     5	
     6	This file contains estimates for the total variation distance between the
     7	uniform distribution on a finite type and the uniform distribution on a
     8	nonempty finite subset, together with averaging bounds for `[0,1]`-valued

    15	namespace MIPStarRE.LDT

    17	/-- Total variation between the uniform distribution on a finite ambient type and
    18	the uniform distribution on a nonempty finite subset.
    19	
    20	This is the elementary finite identity
    21	`TV(uniform α, uniform s) = 1 - |s| / |α|`.  The proof transports the project
    22	`Distribution` statement to Mathlib's uniform probability mass functions. -/
    23	theorem totalVariationDistance_uniformDistribution_uniformOnFinset_eq
    24	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    25	    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty) :
    26	    totalVariationDistance (uniformDistribution α) (Distribution.uniformOnFinset s) =
    27	      1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error) := by
    28	  rw [totalVariationDistance_eq_toPMF_sum]
    29	  change PMF.totalVariationDistance
    30	      ((uniformDistribution α).toPMF (uniformDistribution_isProbability α))
    31	      ((Distribution.uniformOnFinset s).toPMF
    32	        (Distribution.uniformOnFinset_isProbability s hs)) =
    33	    1 - (s.card : Error) / (Fintype.card α : Error)
    34	  rw [uniformDistribution_toPMF, Distribution.uniformOnFinset_toPMF]
    35	  exact PMF.totalVariationDistance_uniformOfFintype_uniformOfFinset_eq s hs
    36	
    37	/-- A `[0,1]`-valued function averaged over a nonempty finite subset is bounded
    38	by its ambient uniform average plus the total variation distance between the
    39	two uniform distributions. -/
    40	theorem avgOver_uniformOnFinset_le_uniformDistribution_add_totalVariationDistance
    41	    {α : Type*} [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nonempty α]
    42	    (s : Finset α) (hs : s.Nonempty)
    43	    (f : α → Error)
    44	    (hf_nonneg : ∀ a, 0 ≤ f a)
    45	    (hf_le_one : ∀ a, f a ≤ 1) :

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: a linear map of the ambient coefficient space

+private theorem isCondLinearOn_one_of_linear {K ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (L : (ι → K) →ₗ[K] (ι → K)) :
+    IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ 1 (fun x => L x) := by
+  refine ⟨.succ Finset.univ L (fun _ i hi => absurd (Finset.mem_univ i) hi)
+      (fun _ => .zero), ⟨Finset.subset_univ _, fun _ => trivial⟩, ?_⟩
+  funext x
+  have hx : coordinateRestriction (Finset.univ : Finset ι) x = x := by
+    funext i
+    simp [coordinateRestriction]
+  show L (coordinateRestriction Finset.univ x) + 0 = L x
+  rw [hx, add_zero]
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: extend a coefficient vector along an injective
+reindexing of registers, setting every coordinate outside the image to zero.
+Together with the lemmas that follow it, this supports the transport of
+conditional linearity between the register spaces of `def:cl-func`,
+blueprint `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:453-463`,
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/05_conditionally_linear_functions.tex:35-57`. -/
+private def clExtend {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] (f : κ → ι) (u : κ → K) : ι → K :=
+  Function.extend f u 0
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension recovers the original
+coordinates along an injective reindexing. -/
+private theorem clExtend_apply {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) (k : κ) :
+    clExtend f u (f k) = u k :=
+  hf.extend_apply u 0 k

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension vanishes at any coordinate
+outside the image of the reindexing. -/
+private theorem clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem {K κ ι : Type*} [Zero K]
+    (f : κ → ι) (u : κ → K) (i : ι) (h : ∀ k, f k ≠ i) :
+    clExtend f u i = 0 :=
+  Function.extend_apply' u (0 : ι → K) i
+    (fun hex => h hex.choose hex.choose_spec)

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: restriction along an injective reindexing

+    (hf : Function.Injective f) (u : κ → K) :

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the extension of the zero vector vanishes. -/

+      obtain ⟨hkS, hkS₁⟩ := Finset.mem_sdiff.mp hk
+      refine Finset.mem_sdiff.mpr ⟨hST (Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hkS), ?_⟩

+      obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
+      exact hkS₁ (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: evaluation commutes with the transport of a
+conditionally linear syntax tree along an injective reindexing. -/
+private theorem clReindexTerm_eval {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) :
+    ∀ {ell : ℕ} (t : CondLinearTerm K (ι := κ) ell) (x : ι → K),
+      CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf t) x =
+        clExtend f (CondLinearTerm.eval t (fun k => x (f k))) := by
+  intro ell t
+  induction t with
+  | zero => intro x; exact (clExtend_zero hf).symm
+  | succ S₁ L₁ hL rest ih =>
+      intro x
+      have hres : (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k)) =
+          coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)) := by
+        funext k
+        by_cases hk : k ∈ S₁
+        · have hmem : f k ∈ S₁.image f := Finset.mem_image_of_mem f hk
+          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hmem]
+        · have hni : f k ∉ S₁.image f := by
+            intro hmem
+            obtain ⟨k', hk', hk'eq⟩ := Finset.mem_image.mp hmem
+            exact hk (hf hk'eq ▸ hk')
+          simp [coordinateRestriction, hk, hni]
+      have hhead : clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) =
+          clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))) := by
+        show clExtend f (L₁ (fun k => coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x (f k))) = _
+        rw [hres]
+      have hcomp : (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
+            (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)) =
+          L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) := by
+        rw [hhead]
+        exact clExtend_comp hf _
+      show clReindexLinear hf L₁ (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) +
+          CondLinearTerm.eval (clReindexTerm hf (rest
+            (fun k => clReindexLinear hf L₁
+              (coordinateRestriction (S₁.image f) x) (f k)))) x =
+        clExtend f (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k))) +
+          CondLinearTerm.eval
+            (rest (L₁ (coordinateRestriction S₁ (fun k => x (f k)))))
+            (fun k => x (f k)))
+      rw [hcomp, ih _ x, hhead, ← clExtend_add hf]
+
+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: conditional linearity is preserved by an
+injective reindexing of registers, the coordinates outside the image of the
+reindexing being set to zero. -/
+private theorem isCondLinearOn_reindex {K κ ι : Type*} [Field K]
+    [Fintype κ] [DecidableEq κ] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] {f : κ → ι}
+    (hf : Function.Injective f) {ell : ℕ} {L : (κ → K) → (κ → K)}
+    (h : IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell L) :
+    IsCondLinearOn K Finset.univ ell
+      (fun x => clExtend f (L (fun k => x (f k)))) := by
+  obtain ⟨t, hsupp, hval⟩ := h
+  refine ⟨clReindexTerm hf t,
+    clReindexTerm_supportedOn hf t Finset.univ Finset.univ hsupp
+      (Finset.subset_univ _), ?_⟩
+  funext x
+  rw [clReindexTerm_eval hf t x, hval]
+

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: the inclusion of the low-degree register index
+into the ambient Pauli register index selected by a basis.  It realizes the
+natural embedding of the range of the low-degree maps described in
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,

+private def pauliLdIndex (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind) :
+    LdIndex P.toLdParams → PauliIndex P

+      | .Z => .inl (.inl (.inl (.inl (.inr j))))

+    Function.Injective (pauliLdIndex P W) := by

+  cases W <;> rcases a with (j | u) | j <;> rcases b with (j' | u') | j' <;>

+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
+private theorem pauliToLd_eq (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (z : PauliSpace P) :

+  funext k

+/-- Formalization-only auxiliary: writing a low-degree vector into the ambient
+Pauli registers is extension along `pauliLdIndex`; see
+`def:pauli-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:285-329`,
+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/
+private theorem embedLd_eq (P : AdmissibleParams) (W : PauliKind)
+    (w : LdSpace P.toLdParams) :
+    embedLd P W w = clExtend (pauliLdIndex P W) w := by
+  have hf := pauliLdIndex_injective P W
+  funext i
+  rcases i with ((((j | j) | u) | j) | u) | u
+  · cases W
+    · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j))).symm
+    · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
+        rintro ((j' | u') | j') <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
+  · cases W
+    · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
+        rintro ((j' | u') | j') <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
+    · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inl (Sum.inl j))).symm
+  · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inl (Sum.inr ()))).symm
+  · exact (clExtend_apply hf w (Sum.inr j)).symm
+  · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
+      intro k
+      cases W <;> rcases k with (j' | u') | j' <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm
+  · exact (clExtend_eq_zero_of_not_mem _ w _ (by
+      intro k
+      cases W <;> rcases k with (j' | u') | j' <;> simp [pauliLdIndex])).symm

+diagonal-line maps are the corresponding low-degree maps reindexed along

+paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1120`. -/

   838

   840	`def:pauli-win-predicate`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:331-367`, paper origin

   860	      | .Z => pauliRZBlock z)) = β

   866	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.

   878	paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:1126-1225`.
   879	-/
   880	noncomputable def pauliWinPredicate (P : AdmissibleParams) :

   892	          if W = W' then decide (pauliAlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   893	      | .dline W, .point W', .dlinePoly f, .value u =>
   894	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xA xB f u) else true
   895	      | .point W, .dline W', .value u, .dlinePoly f =>
   896	          if W = W' then decide (pauliDlinePointCondition P W xB xA f u) else true
   897	      | .point W, .pauli W', .value u, .pauliOutcome h =>
   898	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xA h u) else true
   899	      | .pauli W, .point W', .pauliOutcome h, .value u =>
   900	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPauliCondition P W xB h u) else true

   902	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xA β bits)
   903	      | .pair, .pairW W, .pairBits bits, .bit β =>
   904	          decide (pauliPairCondition P W xB β bits)
   905	      | .point W, .pairW W', .value u, .bit β =>
   906	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xB u β) else true
   907	      | .pairW W, .point W', .bit β, .value u =>
   908	          if W = W' then decide (pauliPointPairCondition P W xA u β) else true

   911	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xA = 0 ∨
   912	              msWinPredicate (.constraint i) (.var j) (.triple β) (.bit γ))

   916	            decide (pauliPairGamma P xB = 0 ∨
   917	              msWinPredicate (.var j) (.constraint i) (.bit γ) (.triple β))

   920	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xB j u β)
   921	      | .ms (.var j), .point W, .bit β, .value u =>
   922	          decide (pauliPointVariableCondition P W xA j u β)

   924	    else false

   929	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:964-1225`.
   930	-/

     4	/-! # Typed conditionally linear distributions
     5	
     6	Typed question distributions first sample an ordered edge of the type graph and
     7	then sample the corresponding pair of conditionally linear images of one common
     8	uniform seed.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:typed-cl-functions` and `def:typed-cl-distributions` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:601-631`, with paper origin
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-94`.

    16	
    17	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    18	
    19	open MIPStarRE.LDT
    20	
    21	/-- A typed family whose member at every type is `ell`-level conditionally
    22	linear. This is `def:typed-cl-functions`, blueprint
    23	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:601-606`, paper
    24	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:57-63`. -/
    25	def IsTypedCondLinearFamily (K T : Type*) [Field K]
    26	    {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    27	    (ell : ℕ) (L : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) : Prop :=
    28	  ∀ t, IsCondLinear ell (L t)
    29	
    30	/-- The typed CL distribution: sample a type pair from the graph distribution,
    31	then bind it to the CL distribution selected by those two types. This is
    32	`def:typed-cl-distributions`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:626-631`, paper
    33	`references/qpbt-paper/07_types.tex:84-94`. -/
    34	noncomputable def typedCLDistribution {K T ι : Type*}
    35	    [Field K] [Fintype K] [DecidableEq K]
    36	    [Fintype T] [DecidableEq T] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    37	    (E : Finset (Sym2 T)) (hE : E.Nonempty)
    38	    (L R : T → (ι → K) → (ι → K)) :
    39	    Distribution ((T × (ι → K)) × (T × (ι → K))) :=
    40	  Distribution.bind (graphDistribution E hE) fun uv =>
    41	    (clDistribution (L uv.1) (R uv.2)).map fun xy =>
    42	      ((uv.1, xy.1), (uv.2, xy.2))

   495	
   496	/-- The question alphabet for the low-degree game (`def:ld-game`, blueprint
   497	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:17-32`; paper origin
   498	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   500	abbrev LdQuestion (P : LdParams) := LdType × LdSpace P
   501	
   502	/-- The typed CL question distribution.  This is the inlined construction in
   503	`def:ld-question-distribution`, blueprint `ch13_qpbt_test.tex:34-59`; paper
   504	origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   505	-/
   506	noncomputable def ldQuestionDistribution (P : LdParams) :
   507	    Distribution (LdQuestion P × LdQuestion P) :=
   508	  Distribution.map
   509	    (uniformDistribution ((LdType × LdType) × LdSpace P))
   510	    (fun s =>
   511	      ((s.1.1, ldCL P s.1.1 s.2), (s.1.2, ldCL P s.1.2 s.2)))
   512	
   513	/-- The coefficient-tuple answer alphabet of the low-degree game.  Polynomial
   514	answers are representatives with exactly the coefficient lengths printed in
   515	the paper, as required by `def:ld-win-predicate` (blueprint
   516	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`; paper
   517	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).
   518	-/
   519	inductive LdAnswer (P : LdParams) where
   520	  | pointVals (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P)
   521	  | alinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   522	  | dlinePolys (a : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   523	  deriving DecidableEq

   528	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.
   529	-/
   530	abbrev LdAnswerCode (P : LdParams) :=
   531	  (Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) ⊕
   532	    ((Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P) ⊕

   537	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   538	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`).

   540	noncomputable def ldAnswerEquiv (P : LdParams) :
   541	    LdAnswer P ≃ LdAnswerCode P where

   544	    | .alinePolys a => .inr (.inl a)
   545	    | .dlinePolys a => .inr (.inr a)

   551	  right_inv := by
   552	    intro x
   553	    cases x with
   554	    | inl a => rfl
   555	    | inr x =>
   556	        cases x with
   557	        | inl a => rfl
   558	        | inr a => rfl

   571	def evalCoefficient {K : Type*} [Semiring K] {n : ℕ}

   584	  | .dline, .dlinePolys _ => true
   585	  | _, _ => false

   592	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   593	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=

   597	    point.point = line.point + t • coordinateDirection (chiIndex P line.seed) →
   598	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

   600	/-- The diagonal line/point relation in `def:ld-win-predicate`, blueprint
   601	`ch13_qpbt_test.tex:137-156`, paper origin
   602	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:31-391`.

   604	def dlinePointCondition (P : LdParams) (line point : LdSpace P)
   605	    (f : Fin P.k → Fin (P.m * P.d + 1) → ScalarQ P)
   606	    (a : Fin P.k → ScalarQ P) : Prop :=
   607	  ∀ t : ScalarQ P,
   608	    point.point = line.point + t • line.direction →
   609	      ∀ j : Fin P.k, evalCoefficient (f j) t = a j

   617	    LdQuestion P → LdQuestion P → LdAnswer P → LdAnswer P → Bool :=

   102	\paragraph{Axis-parallel lines and diagonal lines.}
   103	Before presenting a formal description of the game $\game^\ld$, we first define
   104	what we mean by lines, and their properties.
   105	
   106	\begin{definition}[Lines]
   107	  \label{def:line}
   108		A \emph{line} $\line$ in $\F^m_q$ specified by a pair $(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$
   109	  is the subset
   110	  \begin{equation}
   111	    \label{eq:line-set}
   112	    \line(u,v) = \bigl\{\, u + tv : t \in \F_q \,\bigr\} \subseteq \F_q^m \;.
   113	  \end{equation}
   114	  We call the vector $v$ a \emph{direction} of line
   115	  $\line(u,v)$.\footnote{For convenience we explicitly allow
   116	    $v=0$, in which case the line is reduced to a singleton.}
   117	  
   118	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate $i \in
   119	  \{1,2,\ldots,m\}$ for which $v$ is equal to $e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   120	  vector in $\F_q^m$.
   121	  We say that such a line $\line$ is \emph{parallel to the $i$-th direction}.
   122	  A line $\line(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists an $i \in
   123	  \{0,1,\ldots,m-1\}$ for which $v_1 = v_2 = \cdots = v_i = 0$.
   124	\end{definition}
   125	
   126	The following Proposition establishes that, for a fixed direction, a line
   127	$\line$ is an equivalence class of points on the line.
   128	\begin{proposition}
   129	  \label{prop:line-equiv}
   130	  Let $u,v \in \F_q^m$.
   131	  Then for all $u' \in \line(u,v)$, we have that $\line(u,v) = \line(u',v)$.
   132	\end{proposition}
   133	\begin{proof}
   134		Fix $u' \in \line(u,v)$.
   135	  We have that $u' = u + tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$.
   136	  Let $a \in \line(u,v)$.
   137	  This means that $a = u + sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$.
   138	  We also have that $a = u + (s - t + t)v = u + tv + (s - t)v = u' + (s - t)v$,
   139	  so $\line(u,v) \subseteq \line(u',v)$.
   140	  A similar argument shows that $\line(u',v) \subseteq \line(u,v)$.
   141	\end{proof}
   142	
   143	We now specify a canonical representation of lines $\line = \line(u,v)$ as pairs $(u_0,v)$
   144	where $u_0$ is a \emph{canonical representative} of $\line$ specified as
   145	follows.
   146	Let $L_v^{\lnf}: \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with the
   147	one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$ (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical} for a
   148	definition of canonical linear map).
   149	Note that for all $u \in \line$, we have that $L_v^{\lnf}(u)$ is a point in
   150	$\line$.
   151	This is because since the image and kernel of $L_v^{\lnf}$ are complementary
   152	subspaces by definition (see \Cref{def:cl-canonical}), any $u \in \F_q^m$ has a
   153	unique decomposition $u = u_0 + u_1$ where $u_0$ is in the image of $L_v^{\lnf}$
   154	and $u_1 \in \ker(L_v^{\lnf})$, which by definition is the subspace spanned by
   155	$v$.
   156	Thus $u_1 = tv$ for some $t \in \F_q$ and we have that $u_0 = u - tv \in \line$.
   157	In particular, if $u\in \line$ then $u_0 = L_v^{\lnf}(u) \in \line$ as well. 
   158	Furthermore, since $L_v^{\lnf}$ is a projection onto its image by definition, we
   159	have $L_v^{\lnf}(u_0) = u_0$.
   160	
   161	Next, note that for any $u,u' \in \line$, since $u-u' = sv$ for some $s\in \F_q$
   162	it follows that $L_v^\lnf(u) = L_v^\lnf(u')$.
   163	Thus $u_0 = u_0'$ and this shows that $L_v^\lnf$ gives a means to compute a
   164	canonical representative of lines.
   165	
   166	\begin{definition}[Canonical representative of a line]
   167	  \label{def:line-representative}
   168	  Let $\line$ be a line in direction $v$.
   169	  A canonical representative of $\line$ is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that
   170	  \[
   171	    u_0 = L_v^\lnf(u)
   172	  \]
   173	  for all $u \in \line$.
   174	\end{definition}

   464	\begin{definition}[Lines]\label{def:line}
   465		A \emph{line} $\ell$ in $\F_q^m$ specified by a pair
   466		$(u,v) \in (\F_q^m)^2$ is the subset
   467		\begin{equation}\label{eq:line-set}

   472		line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{axis-parallel} if there is a coordinate
   473		$i \in \{1, \dots, m\}$ for which $v = e_i$, the $i$-th elementary basis
   474		vector of $\F_q^m$; such a line is said to be \emph{parallel to the $i$-th
   475		direction}. A line $\ell(u,v)$ is \emph{diagonal} if there exists
   476		$i \in \{0, 1, \dots, m-1\}$ such that $v_1 = v_2 = \dots = v_i = 0$ (for
   477		$i = 0$ the condition is vacuous, so every line is diagonal).

   503		$L^{\mathrm{Ln}}_v : \F_q^m \to \F_q^m$ denote the canonical linear map with
   504		the one-dimensional kernel basis $\{v\}$

   506		$\ell$} is the point $u_0 \in \F_q^m$ such that

   511		complementary, any $u \in \ell$ decomposes uniquely as $u = u_0 + tv$ with
   512		$u_0$ in the image, so $u_0 = u - tv \in \ell$ and

    25	/--
    26	The affine line through `u` in direction `v`, including the singleton case
    27	`v = 0`.  Blueprint `def:line`, `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`;
    28	paper origin

    31	def linePoints {m : ℕ}
    32	    (u v : Fin m → K) : Set (Fin m → K) :=
    33	  {x | ∃ t : K, x = u + t • v}

    35	/-- The elementary coordinate direction used in the axis-parallel predicate of
    36	`def:line`; blueprint `ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:464-478`, paper origin
    37	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.

    39	def coordinateDirection {m : ℕ}
    40	    (i : Fin m) : Fin m → K :=
    41	  Pi.single i 1
    42	
    43	/--
    44	`IsAxisParallel v` means that `v` is a standard coordinate direction.  This is

    51	/--
    52	The diagonal-direction predicate from `def:line`; a prefix of coordinates may

    54	`references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:106-124`.
    55	-/
    56	def IsDiagonal {m : ℕ} (v : Fin m → K) : Prop :=
    57	  ∃ i : Fin m, ∀ j : Fin m, j.1 < i.1 → v j = 0

    59	/--
    60	Changing the base point to another point on a line leaves the line unchanged.
    61	This is `prop:line-equiv` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:480-486`,
    62	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/08_classical_and_quantum_low_degree_tests.tex:128-132`.

    64	theorem linePoints_eq_of_mem {m : ℕ}
    65	    (u v u' : Fin m → K) (h : u' ∈ linePoints u v) :
    66	    linePoints u v = linePoints u' v := by
    67	  obtain ⟨t, rfl⟩ := h
    68	  ext x
    69	  constructor
    70	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    71	    exact ⟨s - t, by module⟩
    72	  · rintro ⟨s, rfl⟩
    73	    exact ⟨t + s, by module⟩

    75	/--
    76	The canonical linear representative map of a line direction.  It projects onto
    77	the coordinate complement of the span of `v`; for `v = 0` the span is bottom,
    78	so the resulting map is the identity.  Blueprint `def:line-representative`,
    79	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch11_qpbt_algebra.tex:500-520`; paper origin
